title: B300 KDA prefill needs chunk-resident state and stateful native lowering before a scalar route can close the measured gap
backend: native_cuda and cutlass_cute_dsl component admission; B300 adapted CAKE M64 external reference
executor_revision: B300-M4 agent-gpu-broker 0.6.0 custom diagnostic; no formal sm_103a Executor receipt

evidence.note: A separate exact-sm_103a diagnostic port of the pinned B200 CAKE export compiled both M64 and M128 without GPU visibility. Only the host target gate and compilation architecture changed; this is not the original B200 qualification.
M64 fixed H64/T65 full-chunk-plus-tail output 532480/532480 and in-place state 1048576/1048576 passed the independent CPU recurrence at atol=rtol=0.01; all immutable inputs were unchanged.
M128 packed H96 lengths 33,65,17 with seq_order [1,0,2] passed all 1413120 output and 4718592 final-state elements and preserved immutable inputs.
The adapted reference passed the complete H64/T8192 benchmark-shape CPU oracle: 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements, zero tolerance failures, and every immutable input unchanged.

Five broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds with distinct initial-state slots per invocation measured the adapted one-kernel reference at 456.034 microseconds median; maximum within-round CV was 0.117%. Each round retained complete output/state and passed the external CPU oracle. No B200-paper comparison is made.

A direct register-resident per-token native CUDA prototype, outside Compiler admission, passed the complete H64/T65 output and state oracle. NVCC reported 71 registers and zero spills. An earlier host-only target-name refusal was retained as a failed broker job before this successor.
The same native prototype passed every H64/T8192 output and final-state element with unchanged inputs; its correctness cannot establish useful performance.

Five paired broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.195 versus scalar prototype 16979.920 microseconds, median paired scalar/reference 37.220750x. Both arms had exactly one CUDA activity, zero oracle failures and maximum within-round CV 0.135%/0.082%. This is a bounded mechanism diagnostic, not a Cake candidate or formal Evaluation.

Retargeted component probes on sm_103a show simple Triton state source lowers; CuTe state refuses CUTE_STATE_UNSUPPORTED, CuTe TMEM witness refuses CUTE_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED, and native state refuses NATIVE_BUFFER_REFINEMENT_UNSUPPORTED plus load/store ownership refinements. A small native TMA/MMA pipeline witness lowers, but no complete KDA Schedule is admitted.

The committed chunk-32 algebra at dca6ac1d passed all 67108864 output and 1048576 final-state elements against the independent recurrence on the exact H64/T8192 B300 prepared inputs; local BF16-quantized matrix-operand simulation also passed. This validates the mathematical candidate, not its GPU mapping.

An unadmitted one-program-per-head-and-64-V-row Triton chunk-32 prototype compiled for sm_103a. Static cubin inspection reported 128 registers, 176 bytes of stack per thread and 66 local load/store SASS instructions. These facts support a spill/resource-pressure hypothesis, not a dynamic bottleneck attribution.
The unadmitted Triton chunk prototype passed the independent complete H64/T65 output and final-state oracle with immutable inputs unchanged.
The same prototype passed every H64/T8192 output and final-state element at atol=rtol=0.01 with immutable inputs unchanged.

Five paired broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.035 versus unadmitted Triton chunk prototype 96080.520 microseconds, median paired candidate/reference 210.686724x. Both one-kernel arms passed the full oracle each round; maximum within-round CV was 0.108%/0.479%. This negative mechanism diagnostic is neither a qualified Cake candidate nor formal Evaluation.

A smaller unadmitted chunk-16, V-tile-32 Triton variant compiled offline for sm_103a; cubin inspection reported 238 registers, zero stack bytes and no static local SASS accesses. This removes the observed static spill signal but has not established runtime speed.
The smaller variant passed complete H64/T65 output and final-state CPU oracle checks with all immutable inputs unchanged.
The smaller variant also passed all H64/T8192 output and final-state elements at atol=rtol=0.01 with unchanged immutable inputs.

Five same-run broker-exclusive cold-L2 CUPTI rounds measured adapted CAKE reference 456.259 versus unadmitted chunk-16/V-tile-32 Triton 83264.993 microseconds; median paired candidate/reference 182.495015x. Every complete output/state check passed, each arm had one CUDA activity, and maximum within-round CV was 0.144%/0.202%. A predecessor job gpuq-76a2113101cd was refused before launch by the source-commit identity guard and retained as failed evidence. Removing the static spill signal improves latency only modestly; the remaining gap is not uniquely attributed.

Native CUDA's bounded global-state read/modify/write admission at cdaba6c3 passed 47 native contracts and the 179-case Corpus Gate from a clean fixed-commit worktree. An in-place GEMM state Schedule retains one global state argument and checks read-before-MMA-before-store; verifier counterexamples still refuse owner drift and a state store inside the contraction loop. This does not admit KDA's TMEM-resident state.

The emitted native CUDA in-place state witness compiled offline for exact sm_103a with 103 registers and no spills, then passed a broker-shared B300 device check on three independent scales/seeds. Each case matched all 131072 output-state elements within atol=rtol=0.01, changed the caller's state in place and preserved both input matrices. This qualifies a prerequisite mechanism only; it is neither KDA correctness nor KDA performance evidence.

An unadmitted exact-sm_103a native PTX probe packs BF16 row pairs into 32-bit words, writes 128x64 state through tcgen05.st.sync.aligned.32x32b.x8, waits for stores, then reads it through tcgen05.ld and waits for loads. Three 8192-element distributions round-tripped bitwise with input unchanged. Offline NVCC reported 40 registers and zero spills. This proves the isolated register/TMEM copy atom and wait sequence, not tensor-operand MMA or complete KDA state residency.

A separate unadmitted PTX witness packs BF16 state into TMEM, waits for store completion, uses that TMEM tile as tcgen05.mma operand A against a swizzled shared-memory B tile, commits and waits for the MMA, then reads FP32 TMEM output. Three independent 128x64 by 64x64 cases passed all 8192 output elements at atol=rtol=0.01 with maximum absolute error 5.722e-6 and both inputs unchanged. Offline NVCC reported 30 registers, zero stack/spills and an exact-sm_103a cubin. This proves the isolated TMEM-A MMA path on B300, not a KDA chunk update or performance edge.

The isolated task/nvidia-tmem-state-prototype combined the core typed TMEM-store/TMEM-A contract with native CUDA emission and an exact-sm_103a Target declaration. At clean commit e47c78ab, the full CPU contracts passed 2517 tests with 26 skips, and all 179 Corpus Gate cases matched without regenerating expectations. A later documentation-only successor aa5fad67 passed 53 affected tests. This is a local prototype branch; neither its generated source nor its new Target admission has passed NVCC or B300 device validation.

The Compiler emitted a complete single-CTA source from tmem-state-mma-witness on sm_103a: register BF16 load, x8 TMEM store, four-arrival completion, TMA B staging, barrier wait and fence before TMEM-A tcgen05 MMA, FP32 TMEM readout and global store. Public assessment was lowerable and the source was retained for exact-target compilation. Structural emission and CPU contracts are not compile or device evidence.

A two-chunk recurrence-shaped Schedule at fixed compiler e47c78ab tested one pre-loop BF16 TMEM initialization and one in-loop update of the same tensor tile. Common assessment refused BUFFER_MULTIPLE_WRITERS at a_tmem and TMEM_STORE_COMPLETION_OWNERSHIP at state_ready; direct native preflight additionally refused the loop pipeline body, TMEM-A contraction scope, completion consumer lifetime and in-loop TMEM store. The retained schedule isolates a missing loop-carried state effect and per-chunk barrier phase for this route; it does not prove every possible Cake formulation impossible.

observation: The new B300 KDA prefill Workload and independent BF16 recurrence oracle are committed at c0486915 and 6b7d99ec; the original six-row B200 task remains unchanged. A minimally adapted pinned CAKE M64/M128 reference compiles and passes fixed, packed and full H64/T8192 output/state checks on B300-M4. The H64/T8192 adapted reference has a stable approximately 456 us single-kernel diagnostic baseline. The committed chunk-32 recurrence algebra passes the complete CPU oracle, including a BF16-quantized operand simulation. A correct register-resident per-token native prototype is 37.220750x slower, while unadmitted chunk-32/V-tile-64 and chunk-16/V-tile-32 Triton prototypes are 210.686724x and 182.495015x slower in separate same-run comparisons. The larger Triton variant uses 176 bytes of stack per thread; the smaller variant has zero stack and no static local SASS accesses but still takes 83.265 ms. This comparison changes several tile parameters together, so it does not isolate a spill penalty; serial chunk mapping and duplicated work remain hypotheses without dynamic counters. Neither direct scalar CUDA nor either large-live-tensor Triton mapping closes the gap. The reference emission visibly uses 32-token chunks, five-slot producer/compute/epilogue pipeline, TMA, tcgen05 MMA and TMEM-resident state. The native backend now admits a bounded global state read/modify/write Schedule and has B300 device evidence for that prerequisite. Two unadmitted PTX probes prove BF16 register/TMEM roundtrip and TMEM-A tcgen05 MMA numerics on exact B300. Separate core and NVIDIA prototype task branches now type and emit a single root TMEM-A contraction and pass CPU contracts and Corpus Gate, but generated-source NVCC/device qualification remains absent. A two-chunk probe localizes the next expressibility gap to loop-carried TMEM writers and their barrier phases, with corresponding native pipeline and lifetime refusals. No full typed Cake KDA candidate, six-shape B300 comparison, framework validation or formal Evaluation exists yet.
proposed_change: Build one complete H64 fixed-shape Schedule whose concrete storage and access commitments name state ownership, ordered 32-token chunks, TMEM state residency, TMA descriptor boxes, tcgen05 instruction atoms, five-role pipeline and synchronization. The next shared IR tick must state which TMEM buffer is carried across chunk iterations, distinguish its pre-loop initializer from its per-iteration writer, and prove the producer/consumer mbarrier phase before the native backend lowers it; the two-chunk probe supplies the first counterexample. Before emission, check P1-P8 and extend the owning common IR typing/effects, verifier legality and native CUDA lowering in one successor change; existing backends must refuse unsupported state/chunk commitments by name. Keep the reference as an external black-box baseline rather than an opaque backend escape. Qualify the successor first against the fixed T65 guardrail and full H64/T8192 output/state oracle, then paired B300-M4 CUPTI and profiler evidence; only after a strong seed extend to M128 packed and all six rows. An automatic estimate or the scalar prototype does not authorize promotion. Formal Executor admission and branch integration remain separate gates.
